newsitem.title: SPAIN: Bank of Spain's Malo sees inflation declining more.
newsitem.headline: Bank of Spain's Malo sees inflation declining more.

text.p: Bank of Spain's Jose Luis Malo de Molina said on Tuesday that he saw Spanish inflation continuing to trend downward.
Spanish consumer inflation declined to 3.6 percent in September from 3.7 percent in August and the Spanish government is shooting for 3.5 percent at year-end.
"The current outlook points toward continuity in the process of decline (in inflation)," Malo de Molina said at a seminar here.

Malo added that the low rate of growth of imported products, improved behaviour of some foodstuffs and exchange rate stability suggested that the light rise in inflation over the summer was temporary.
Nonetheless, he said there were risks.

The rise in energy prices could have a negative effect on inflation and the current wage pacts are incompatible "not just with a future reduction in inflation, but also with the maintenance of current levels," he said.
He noted Spain's inflation average had to drop 1.3 points still to reach the range required by Maastricht for participation in Europe's common currency launch.
"The risks that there are deviations are not insignificant," Malo said.
Nonetheless, he was confident that Spain could reach its ambitious goals for 1997.
Malo also pointed out that Spain had made important progress in reducing most of its major desequilibriums, from the deficit and the high rates of employment.
